10.1002_adma.202512568: Ruthenium (Ru)‐based dual‐site catalysts can efficiently accelerate alkaline hydrogen electrocatalytic kinetics by virtue of the well‐balanced competitive adsorptions of multiple reaction intermediates. However, their insufficient mass transfer makes them far away from the applications, largely lying to the challenge of precisely manipulating the interface water structure. Herein, a concept of nitrogen‐bridged positively charged dual sites with a robust interfacial hydrogen‐bond network is presented for enhancing alkaline hydrogen oxidation and evolution reactions (HOR and HER). The positively charged Ru and Ni sites are demonstrated to trigger the ordered water orientation with the favorable “O‐down” configuration, strengthening the interfacial hydrogen‐bond network and promoting the mass transfer. In particular, the efficient charge‐transfer channels of asymmetric Ru‐N‐Ni bridges can maintain the high‐valence of Ru sites and high electron density of Ni sites, thus stabilizing * OH adsorption on Ru sites and weakening * H adsorption on Ni sites, as well as enhancing anti‐CO poisoning ability. As a result, the elaborated Ru‐Ni 3 N catalysts achieve a mass activity of 60.6 A g −1 for HOR, representing one of the most active one among state‐of‐the‐art Ru‐based catalysts yet reported. This interfacial hydrogen‐bond network modulation strategy can also be extended to HER electrocatalysis, driving the anion exchange membrane water electrolyzer to achieve a low cell voltage of 1.79 V at 1 A cm −2 and excellent long‐term stability at an industrial current density of 500 mA cm −2 for more than 550 h.
10.1002_adma.73445: Although chalcogenide‐based catalysts offer significant potential for enhancing lithium‐sulfur (Li‐S) battery performance, the absence of reliable descriptors linking the d ‐band center to sulfur conversion kinetics hinders the rational design of electrochemical systems. Herein, we address this limitation by engineering a catalytic interlayer through modification of 2H‐MoS 2 electronic structure, achieved via substitutional doping of n‐type Co/Fe transition metals (TM) at Mo sites. Comprehensive findings elucidate that such doping initiates a distinct S‐mediated d ‐ p hybridization involving Mo 4 d— S 3 p— TM 3 d orbitals, thereby modulating electronic density of states near the Fermi level. Specifically, in the CoFe‐MoS 2 @carbon paper (CP) interlayer, synergistic effect of co‐doping with two different TM drives optimized downshift of the Mo 4 d ‐band center to intermediate energy states, fostering moderate catalyst‐reactant interaction. Furthermore, the simultaneously lowered S 3 p ‐band center enhances the degree of d ‐ p orbital overlap. These electronic redistributions enhance both electrical and ionic conductivity, thereby facilitating accelerated redox kinetics with reduced activation energy, while mitigating the shuttle effect and promoting uniform Li 2 S deposition. Consequently, the assembled cell delivers outstanding stability with a low decay rate of 0.024% for 2000 cycles even at 10C. This work emphasizes that a balanced d ‐band center is key to achieving highly active chalcogenide‐based materials for advanced Li‐S batteries.
10.1016_j.coelec.2026.101864: Electrochemical sensors are important analytical tools due to their sensitivity, low reagent consumption, and compatibility with portable and miniaturized devices. These characteristics make them attractive for environmental monitoring, clinical diagnostics, forensic and food analyses. However, conventional electrochemical sensors rely on non-renewable materials, synthetic polymers, and fabrication processes that contribute to material consumption and waste generation. As demand for low-cost and disposable devices increases, improving the sustainability of electrochemical sensors has become an important research direction. This perspective summarizes advances in sustainable materials and green fabrication strategies. Renewable substrates such as cellulose and biomass-derived conductive materials are discussed as promising alternatives. 3D-printing technology enables material-efficient fabrication and the use of recyclable and bio-based polymers. Current challenges include variability of bio-derived materials, limitations in mechanical and electrochemical stability, and the need to balance sustainability with electroanalytical performance. These developments highlight the role of sustainable materials in environmentally responsible electrochemical sensors design.
10.1016_j.envint.2026.110588: Microplastics and heavy metals are ubiquitous co-contaminants in aquatic environments, yet their combined immunotoxic effects remain poorly understood. This study investigated the individual and combined toxicities of LDPE microplastics and ZnSO 4 in zebrafish across multiple biological levels. LDPE-associated material accumulated mainly in the gastrointestinal tract and liver, with ZnSO 4 co-exposure possibly influencing hepatic retention. Co-exposure exacerbated developmental toxicity, reducing survival, body length, and hatching rate while increasing malformations. In larvae, LDPE induced concentration-dependent ROS bursts; in adults, chronic exposure reduced ROS, with co-exposure restoring control levels. Apoptosis and neutrophil dynamics showed time- and concentration-dependent biphasic patterns. Flow cytometry revealed persistent erythroid and myeloid expansions, lymphocyte depletion, and precursor cell alterations. Transcriptomic profiling showed that LDPE alone enriched the ubiquitin–proteasome pathway, whereas co-exposure was associated with a shift toward sphingolipid/retinol metabolism, C-type lectin receptor signaling, and ferroptosis, accompanied by persistent inflammatory signatures. These findings indicate that ZnSO 4 co-exposure is associated with a shift in the LDPE response from acute proteotoxic stress toward sustained immune modulation, which may affect host immune competence. This study provides novel insights into the immunotoxicological risks of combined microplastic–heavy metal pollution.
10.1021_acscatal.6c01652: The spin state of metal centers is a pivotal yet underexploited descriptor for electrocatalysis. This challenge is acute in bifunctional oxygen electrocatalysts, where the desirable high-spin state for optimal intermediate adsorption on single-atom sites is difficult to achieve and further complicated by the concurrent need to stabilize co-existing metallic nanoparticles against sintering. We propose that geometric distortion can serve as a driver to simultaneously distort single-atom sites and suppress nanoparticle sintering. To demonstrate this, we developed a poly(ionic liquid)-confined ultrafast thermal shock synthesis. Applied to a cobalt–nitrogen–carbon system, this strategy induces geometric distortion in Co-N4 moieties, triggering a low-to-intermediate-spin transition and simultaneously suppressing Co NP agglomeration. Combined spectroscopic, magnetic, and theoretical analyses confirm that this distortion downshifts the d-band center, optimizes orbital overlap with oxygen intermediates, and lowers reaction barriers. The optimized catalyst exhibits high bifunctional activity (ORR E1/2 = 0.84 V; OER η = 366 mV at 20 mA cm−2), delivers a peak power density of 312 mW cm−2, and retains its structure after ∼1360 charge–discharge cycles in a zinc-air battery. This work establishes geometric-distortion-driven spin-state modulation as a generalizable and actionable design principle for advanced electrocatalysts.
10.1021_jacs.5c15943: Sodium-ion batteries are promising energy storage device candidates, yet are limited by low energy density. NaNi 0.33 Fe 0.33 Mn 0.33 O 2 (NFM) activates oxygen redox under high voltage and delivers a high capacity, but suffers from irreversible oxygen loss and rapid capacity fading. Moreover, the underlying failure mechanism is still debatable. Herein, we highlight the critical role of Fe migration in NFM electrochemical degradation and develop approaches to suppress Fe migration and facilitate reversible oxygen redox. Incorporating Ca and Sn into NFM mitigates the OP2 phase, alleviates NiO 6 /FeO 6 Jahn–Teller distortions, and deters incoming Fe 3+ ions. Consequently, the out-of-plane Fe migration is effectively suppressed, thus minimizing undercoordinated oxygen species formation and achieving highly reversible oxygen redox. As-optimized NFM cathode exhibits a high capacity of 158.3 mAh g –1 and excellent electrochemical stability even under high voltage (4.5 V) and high temperature (50 °C). The pouch cells using this NFM cathode achieve a high capacity retention of 80.7% after 2000 cycles. This interlayer-migration-free cathode offers guidelines for developing long-life sodium-ion layered oxides.
10.1039_d5ta08125d: An atomically precise quantity of zinc( ii ) doping into the MnWO 4 lattice localizes the valence-band charge at the manganese sites to enhance the anodic capability and selectivity of the ammonia oxidation reaction (AOR) towards nitrate formation.
